items.text: MEE014 will look into rechargeable batteries for the remote.
MEE014 will consider a port and an alarm to prevent loss.
UI will check the financial feasibility of incorporating voice recognition.
UI will evaluate the option of using a whistle if voice recognition is not feasible.
Voice recognition will be left out of the design.
A flip design will be used.
The remote will have a shell with a shape different from what's normal.
Kinetic charging will be adopted and will use watch-type batteries.
LCD display on the top side of the flip top, rubberised buttons on the bottom, two separate PCBs joined by cabling, and a plastic case with fruit/vegetable-coloured rubber cover.
Battery size between double-A and triple-A remains to be decided.
Voice recognition feasibility will determine whether to implement or fallback to a whistle.
Maintain the central button pattern for volume and channel and keep it standard across models.
Cost feasibility of voice recognition is uncertain and may force changes.
LCD display is not cheap.

abstracts.text: MEE014 will look into rechargeable batteries for the remote and will consider a port and an alarm to prevent loss.
UI will assess the financial feasibility of incorporating voice recognition and will evaluate the option of using a whistle if voice recognition is not feasible.

A series of design decisions were established: voice recognition will be left out, a flip design will be used, the remote will have a shell with a shape different from what's normal, and kinetic charging using watch-type batteries will be adopted.
LCD display on the top side of the flip top, rubberised buttons on the bottom, two separate PCBs joined by cabling, and a plastic case with a fruit/vegetable-coloured rubber cover were decided.

Battery size between double-A and triple-A remains to be decided; the central button pattern for volume and channel will be maintained across models, and cost and LCD display affordability are ongoing concerns.
